questions.question: In a certain language FASHION is coded as FOIHSAN. How is PROBLEM coded in that code?
questions.questionHtml: In a certain language FASHION is coded as FOIHSAN. How is PROBLEM coded in that code?
questions.solution:
From FASHION → FOIHSAN, the first and last letters stay the same (F and N), and the middle part “ASHIO” is reversed to “OIHSA”.

Apply the same rule to PROBLEM: keep P and M fixed; reverse the middle “ROBLE” → “ELBOR”.

So, the code is PELBORM.

questions.question: Among D, F, J, P, and A, who reached office last? Statement I. F and J reached office together. II. Only D and P reached office ahead of J.
questions.questionHtml:
Among D, F, J, P, and A, who reached office last?

Statement

I. F and J reached office together.
II. Only D and P reached office ahead of J.

options.text: Data in statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
options.html: Data in statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

options.text: Data in statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
options.html: Data in statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

options.text: Data in either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question.
options.html: Data in either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question.

options.text: Data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question.
options.html: Data in both statements I and II together are necessary to answer the question.

questions.solution:
From I and II, we conclude that only D and P reached office ahead of J and thus, F. This implies that A reached last.

So, the data in both I and II together are required to answer the given question.

questions.question: Statements: Some taxis have horns. Some taxis have lights. Conclusions: I. Every taxi has either horn or light. II. Some taxis have neither light nor horn. III. Some taxis have horns as well as lights. IV. No taxi has horn as well as light.
questions.questionHtml:
Statements:
Some taxis have horns. Some taxis have lights.

Conclusions:
I. Every taxi has either horn or light.
II. Some taxis have neither light nor horn.
III. Some taxis have horns as well as lights.
IV. No taxi has horn as well as light.
questions.solution:
Conclusion I:

"Every taxi has either horn or light" → This is a universal affirmative statement.

❌ Not valid, because the statements only talk about "some" taxis, not "all".

Conclusion II:

"Some taxis have neither light nor horn" → This is a possibility, but not definitely true from the given statements.

❌ Not valid, as it does not follow directly.

Conclusion III:

"Some taxis have horns as well as lights" → This is a possibility, but not certain from the given statements.

❌ Not valid, as it does not follow directly.

Conclusion IV:

"No taxi has horn as well as light" → This is a universal negative statement.

❌ Not valid, as it contradicts possibility and is not supported by the given data.

Final Answer: None of the conclusions follow.
